before: Every placement follows the same sequence: choose an available Tile and a reachable empty hex; check terrain, adjacency and the Tile’s printed placement rule; pay the cost; then place the Tile and resolve its placement effect. The Vale contains Grasslands, Woodland, Arable Land, Mountains, Heaths, Ruins and Water/River terrain. Use the map legend below to identify each region. Read printed requirements exactly: Mine Tunnel goes on Mountains, Farmstead on Arable Land, Salvage Camp on Ruins and Bridge on Water/River. Shelter in the Ruins: when placing or upgrading a Tile whose entire footprint lies on Ruins, ignore all Stone in that cost. If any part of the footprint lies outside Ruins, pay the full printed cost. Any Land means an empty non-Water/River hex unless the Tile says otherwise.
after:
To place a Tile, choose an available Tile and a reachable empty hex. Check terrain, adjacency and the Tile’s printed placement rule, pay its cost, then place it and resolve any placement effect.

The Vale has seven terrains: Grasslands, Woodland, Arable Land, Mountains, Heaths, Ruins and Water/River. Use the map legend to identify them. Read each placement requirement exactly: Mine Tunnel goes on Mountains, Farmstead on Arable Land, Salvage Camp on Ruins and Bridge on Water/River. Any Land means an empty non-Water/River hex unless the Tile says otherwise.

Shelter in the Ruins: when placing or upgrading a Tile whose entire footprint lies on Ruins, ignore all Stone in that cost. If any part of its footprint lies outside Ruins, pay the full printed cost.

before: To resolve Linked Production, check the chosen Resource Tile and its immediately adjacent copies from the same Tile stack. If none has participated in Linked Production this round, the chosen Tile and every immediately adjacent, non-Overstrained copy produce for that single Activate Action. Use each producer’s current side. Linked Production does not continue outward through a chain.
after:
To resolve Linked Production, check the chosen Resource Tile and every immediately adjacent copy from the same Tile stack. If none has participated this round, the chosen Tile and all immediately adjacent, non-Overstrained copies produce for that one Activate Action. Use each producer’s current side.

Linked Production does not continue outward through a chain. Check only the copies immediately adjacent to the chosen Tile.

A disconnected matching set may still use its own Linked Production. All participation refreshes at the start of the next round.
after: Mark every Tile that produced as having participated this round. If the chosen Tile or any immediately adjacent matching Tile has already participated, only the chosen Tile produces. before: Boons help the settlement. Read the row for the current Season and resolve it immediately unless the italic line tells you to keep the card face up. A kept Boon remains active until used or until its printed duration ends, then discard it. Using a face-up Boon costs no Action unless its text says otherwise. For example, A Little Time adds 1 timer to an active Arrival in Season I, up to 3; its later Season rows add up to 2 or 3 timers as printed. Only one Boon may modify a single Action unless a rule says otherwise.
after:

before: Resolve a Burden by paying and performing its printed resolution, usually with an Interact Action, or by using an effect that explicitly resolves it. For example, Old Wounds Reopen asks you to choose Social/Wellbeing Tiles, then pay Herbs or take Strain; its italic line states the Action and payment needed to discard it. If a Burden offers payment or Strain, choose the branch before drawing a Target Card and draw only for the Strain branch. Resolving a Burden prevents future reapplication but does not remove Strain already placed.
after:
Resolve a Burden by paying and performing its printed resolution, usually with an Interact Action, or by using an effect that explicitly resolves it. For example, Old Wounds Reopen asks you to choose Social/Wellbeing Tiles, then pay Herbs or take Strain. Its italic line gives the Action and payment needed to discard it.

If a Burden offers payment or Strain, choose the branch before drawing a Target Card. Draw only for the Strain branch. Resolving the Burden stops future reapplication; Strain it has already placed remains.

before: Arrivals are timed objectives that unlock Special Tiles. When one is revealed, place it face up with 3 timer tokens, one in each circle. Quiet Quest, for example, requires 4 Goods and 2 Herbs and unlocks Special Tile 1, the Adventurers’ Guild. To complete an Arrival, meet its Requirements and spend 1 Interact Action before its final timer is removed. Remove its timers, discard it and set the unlocked Special Tile beside the board. Any player may later place that Tile with a normal Place Action, following its printed placement rule and paying 0 resources. An activated Inn adds 1 timer to an active Arrival; Dawn Break Inn adds up to 2. An Arrival can never hold more than 3 timers.
after:

before: Supported prevents 1 Strain before you check whether a Tile becomes Overstrained. A Tile either has Supported or does not; passive and single-use Supported never stack. Common Land gives passive Supported to 1 adjacent Housing Tile; The Pleasance gives it to up to 3. Choose the eligible Housing Tiles when the effect becomes active. Keep those choices until the eligible set changes or the source becomes Overstrained, then choose again when required. Passive Supported cannot be reassigned in response to incoming Strain. Supported granted by placement, activation or another effect is single-use unless the rule says it is passive.

before: The Steward’s Ledger tracks achievements across games. Before your group’s first game, choose a name and an unused Roman numeral (I–VI) in the Group Register. Use that numeral for every Entry mark and Game Record. After scoring, mark NAMED for each newly completed Entry and record the shared final score and those Entries. Each NAMED mark counts once toward Golden milestones; player-count prestige marks are records only. Completed Entries are never spent or reset. An AFTER gate is met only if the group begins the game with the shown number of Named Entries.

before: Tiles are adjacent when their hexes share a side; a corner touch is not adjacency. Placement markers such as ADJ. HOUSING, ADJ. TRAVEL and ADJ. RIVER use this side-sharing rule. Adjacency is different from reachability: a Tile can be reachable through the connected settlement network without being adjacent. All side-adjacent, non-Overstrained Tiles form that network.
after: Tiles are adjacent when their hexes share a side. Touching at a corner is not adjacency. Requirements such as ADJ. HOUSING, ADJ. TRAVEL and ADJ. RIVER use this side-sharing rule. A Tile may be reachable through the settlement network without being adjacent. All side-adjacent, non-Overstrained Tiles form that network.
